- ORAL TREPONEME ENRICHMENT BROTH (OTEB)

- Products: AS-603 Oral Treponeme Enrichment Broth (OTEB) 10 tubes / pkg
Intended Use: OTEB is an enriched medium for the isolation, cultivation and maintenance of Treponemes found as part of the oral flora.

OTEB is a complex peptone-yeast extract medium containing volatile fatty acids and serum for a source of long chain fatty acids. Volatile fatty acids and serum are necessary nutrients for recovery of Treponemes from the oral flora. Inoculation of the medium can be done using a gassing cannula or inside an anaerobic chamber. This medium is prepared, stored and dispensed under oxygen-free conditions to prevent the formation of oxidized products prior to use.

Superseded historical provenance, not a current formulation claim:
Commercial Product: LB Medium (Luria-Bertani, Miller formulation)
Supplier: Multiple suppliers (Difco, Sigma, etc.)
Catalog: Multiple (L3522 Sigma, 244520 BD)
Source: https://www.laboratorynotes.com/preparation-of-luria-bertani-lb-miller-broth/
Accessed: 2026-03-28

Constituent composition researched from product specification.

Preserve source descriptive/preparation text without falsely encoding every paragraph as an instruction: OTEB-medium is available from Anaerobe Systems (http://www.anaerobesystems.com)
The following text was taken from the above page: 

- ORAL TREPONEME ENRICHMENT BROTH (OTEB)

- Products: AS-603 Oral Treponeme Enrichment Broth (OTEB) 10 tubes / pkg
Intended Use: OTEB is an enriched medium for the isolation, cultivation and maintenance of Treponemes found as part of the oral flora.
OTEB is a complex peptone-yeast extract medium containing volatile fatty acids and serum for a source of long chain fatty acids. Volatile fatty acids and serum are necessary nutrients for recovery of Treponemes from the oral flora. Inoculation of the medium can be done using a gassing cannula or inside an anaerobic chamber. This medium is prepared, stored and dispensed under oxygen-free conditions to prevent the formation of oxidized products prior to use.
Final pH 7.0 +/- 0.2 at 25 degrees C.
Final volume 7.0 ml +/- 0.7.

The original states final pH 7.0 +/- 0.2 at 25 C: the range 6.8-7.2 remains, while 25 C is a measurement condition. The printed final volume 7.0 +/- 0.7 ml is retained, but cannot establish this formula's batch denominator. The API declares 1000 ml although listed liquid inputs sum to 1003.1 ml. No final-medium g/L or density conversion is inferred.

Complete source tables were inspected. Reconstructed ingredient/stock nodes retain source-specific amounts and uncertainties; historical flattened amounts, false supplier-tagged LB ingredients and unsupported interpretations are archived in append-only history. Existing unrelated metadata and prior evidence remain preserved, not recertified.
